name: Fatal Mitochondrial Disease Due to Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 3

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Early onset progressive encephalopathy with lactic acidosis
Deficiency of multiple respiratory chain enzyme complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes affecting oxidative phosphorylation
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia and brainstem abnormalities
Elevated blood and CSF lactate levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early onset progressive encephalopathy with lactic acidosis, biochemical evidence of multiple respiratory chain deficiencies, and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic variability.

searchTerms: progressive brain disease with skill loss
worsening brain function and developmental decline
very high lactic acid in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Combined deficiency of multiple respiratory chain complexes
searchTerms: lack of multiple mitochondrial respiratory enzymes
endocrine disorders with high blood sugar

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate
Multiple respiratory chain enzyme complex deficiencies in muscle biopsy
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia, brainstem, and cerebral white matter abnormalities
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) showing lactate peak
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation proteins (e.g., SCO2, SURF1, or others depending on subtype)
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondria on electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly affects basal ganglia with characteristic MRI lesions
Usually caused by mutations in mitochondrial or nuclear genes but with distinct clinical course
May have elevated lactate but less commonly combined respiratory chain defects
Presence of stroke-like episodes and characteristic mitochondrial DNA mutations
Onset typically in childhood or young adulthood
Distinctive clinical features such as migraine-like headaches and seizures

redFlags: Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Multisystem involvement with combined respiratory chain deficiencies
references: Rahman S, et al. Mitochondrial disease due to combined oxidative phosphorylation defects. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2017;40(4):527-537.
Orphanet: Combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency type 3. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003;348(26):2656-2668.
